title: Bootstrap sequence and stateful init: bare-metal + vSphere sketch
content:
Purpose:

This is a working sketch for a repeatable on-prem cluster bootstrap sequence that covers two primary deployment substrates we run into: bare-metal flings (PXE + iSCSI/dual-NIC) and vSphere-based clusters (VM templates + cloud-init). The focus is on sequence ordering to safely bring up control plane components, register stateful workloads, and provide a low-risk upgrade path for minor kube upgrades and CSI/storage transitions.

Audience:
- Platform engineers doing customer Private deployments
- Solutions engineers preparing handoff materials for customers
- Release engineers validating bootstrap modules

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Deterministic bootstrap order that tolerates partial failures
- Idempotent Terraform/Terraform-module operations for node pools and networking
- Safe stateful initialization: ensure PVs and databases are recovered in order
- Clear rollback/rollback-window and post-upgrade validation hooks

Assumptions & constraints:
- Customers may be air-gapped; artifact delivery is via local registry or mirrored buckets
- We support two main provisioning paths: PXE (bare metal) and vSphere template-based instantiation
- External services (DNS, AD/Kerberos, NTP) may be preexisting or temporarily emulated
- Storage variants: local-disk (hostPath/LVM), iSCSI/CEPH/RBD, vSphere CSI (VMDK), and enterprise arrays

Bootstrap sequence (recommended order) - lean version:
1) Pre-flight checks (see checklist block)
2) Provision network, DHCP/TFTP, and IPAM reservations (Terraform)
3) Boot control-plane nodes (PXE or VM), ensure kubeadm/token-based join secret is available
4) Initialize etcd/control-plane (single-master or HA control plane)
5) Bring up CNI and core services (CoreDNS, kube-proxy)
6) Register storage classes and install CSI drivers (in read-only mode if supported)
7) Bring up stateful infra (etcd-operator if used, Postgres clusters, messaging) with init ordering
8) Scale worker pools and join workers
9) Run admission controllers, RBAC policies, and cluster-wide CRDs
10) Start customer workloads, monitor steady-state

Detailed pre-flight checklist (run locally before any apply)
- Inventory: node MACs, serials, intended roles, rack/rack-unit mapping
- Validate DHCP scopes and TFTP images for PXE hosts
- Verify vSphere templates: flavor, cloud-init config, sysprep scripts
- Ensure local registry image set uploaded (images manifest + sha list)
- Validate storage backends for CSI (credentials, endpoints, lun mapping)
- KMS/HSM access checked for secrets if using encrypted volumes
- Terraform state lock backends reachable (s3/minio with locking, consul, etcd)
- Slack/Oncall rotation updated, pager duty escalation ready

Terraform module notes (opinionated)
- Module layout suggestion:
  - module.networking (VLANs, IPAM reservations, load-balancer objects)
  - module.bootimages (PXE images, tftp/ignition blobs, vsphere templates reference)
  - module.control_plane (vm/resource definitions, cloud-init, kubeadm tokens)
  - module.workers (node pools, labels, taints, autoscaling groups if supported)
  - module.storage (CSI secrets, storageclass objects, provisioner credentials)
  - module.postdeploy (helm_release/manifest_apply hooks for core infra)

- Idempotency & partial apply patterns:
  - Avoid long-running boots inside Terraform. Terraform should create resources until the VM exists and returns an IP; use external/local-exec to register a job that signals a separate orchestration service (e.g., a bootstrap-controller) to continue the install.
  - Use null_resource triggers + remote-exec sparingly. Prefer a two-phase apply: infra-first, then orchestration-phase (k8s manifests via CI pipeline).
  - Backends: enforce state locking (s3 + DynamoDB or consul). Document manual unlock playbook for P0 incidents.

- Variables to expose from modules (minimum useful set):
  - admin_cidrs, control_plane_count, worker_pools (list), image_set_ref, pxe_boot_profile, vsphere_template_id, storage_backend_type, csi_enable_features (list)

Stateful init & PV concerns
- PV recovery order matters: DB master before read-only caches. Helm charts should include pre-install hooks that check PV readiness but avoid creating PVCs that bind to the wrong storage class.
- Strategy: create StorageClass objects first in a disabled-binding mode where possible (enable volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer). Then install CSI driver in preview mode (no dynamic provisioning) and validate LUNs/volumes. Once driver and identity checks pass, flip the annotation/flag to enable provisioning.
- For vSphere: ensure proper VM UUID passthrough and tag-based backing to avoid storage orphaning during vSphere scale/clone operations. Collect and store vSphere volume IDs in a migration map if moving from raw vmfs to VMDK.

Rolling upgrade plan (small version jumps, e.g., 1.23.x -> 1.24.3)
- Pre-upgrade: run kube-bench and conformance smoke tests in a staging clone; run data-plane performance baseline with short synthetic traces
- Stage 0 (control plane minor upgrade):
  - Drain non-critical master workloads, upgrade kube-apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler sequentially (one control-plane node at a time for HA clusters)
  - Validate API response times and core metrics for 15–30 minutes
- Stage 1 (CSI + storage driver):
  - Upgrade CSI driver in canary namespace using a small set of test PVCs and pods; verify attach/detach and I/O stability
- Stage 2 (worker rotation):
  - Rotate workers in small batches (5–10% of capacity), ensuring PodDisruptionBudgets allow desired eviction rate
  - For stateful sets with partitioned rollout, prefer in-place kubelet upgrade where possible, otherwise create replacement nodes and cordon old ones
- Post-upgrade validation:
  - Run perf and correctness smoke suite, run logs for controller restarts, and validate Prometheus alerting thresholds

Rollback & emergency steps
- If control-plane fails to reach steady-state after an upgrade step:
  - Revert kube-apiserver/controller-manager binaries to previous image tag via image-rollback channel and restart component pods
  - If leader election stalemates occur, use etcdctl snapshot restore from last healthy snapshot (document S3/minio snapshot path and retention policy)
- For worker-level regressions: annotate Node objects to prevent scheduling, scale previous nodepool back up (if backed by vsphere template) and reattach PVCs using vSphere volumeMap mapping

Operational gotchas (lessons learned)
- Dual-NIC boot order on older BMC firmware can cause incorrect IP assignment on first boot — we created a 30s boot-delay hook in PXE templates to avoid NIC race.
- vSphere templates must have a consistent machine-id and cloud-init secrets to prevent identical node identity which breaks kubelet identity checks. Add a machine-id rewrite step in the template build pipeline.
- CSI migration: when migrating storageclasses (e.g., in-tree to CSI), create new StorageClass names and perform application-level drain to control attachment semantics instead of renaming classes in-place.

Checks during failovers and handoffs
- Sanity: kubectl get cs, nodes, pods -A | grep NotReady and kube-system restarts > 1 in 5m
- Data: verify DB replication lag, missing WAL segments, or volume re-attachment errors in vSphere events
- Networking: run simple e2e flow from replica pod to cluster-external IP to validate SNAT/routing

Open questions / decisions to make
- Should Terraform manage helm releases for core infra (CSI, CNI) or should we shift all k8s manifests into the pipeline after infra apply? Tradeoff: single source vs different rollback semantics.
- How do we standardize a safe default for storageclass migration at scale across multiple customers with different arrays?
- Granularity of nodepool definitions: many small nodepools give better isolation for upgrades but increase provisioning complexity and licensing counts in vSphere.

Next steps (short-term):
- Convert this sketch into a two-page runbook and a 1:1 checklist for field engineers
- Add a small integration test harness in infra repo that exercises the two-phase apply (create VMs -> trigger bootstrap-controller -> validate CSI attach)
- Gather sample tracing from last three customer onprem installs and extract top-5 failure modes to include in a final playbook

Appendix A: quick PXE & vSphere diff notes
- PXE: stateless images, iPXE scripts, DHCP/TFTP dependencies, requires rack-level access, low-cost but fragile firmware interactions
- vSphere: fast templated instantiation, vCenter automation, easier snapshot/rollback, licensing/cost overhead, must handle UUID and disk cloning semantics

Appendix B: minimal backout commands (cheat sheet)
- Terraform: terraform state pull | jq . to inspect, terraform force-unlock <lock-id>
- etcd: etcdctl snapshot save /restore --endpoints=<endpoints> --cacert=...
- vSphere: govc disk.change -vm <vm> -disk.label <disk> -path <vmdk> to reattach if mapping broke

Notes to self: capture example cloud-init snippets and a PXE ipxe menu fragment next pass. Also check Marco's notes (linked PR) about machine-id rewriting as a templating step.

-- end of sketch --
